title: Between-phonation perturbation dispersion does not improve fixed-model Parkinson classification across two public voice cohorts
abstract: A fixed model trained on 32 Oxford voice subject codes was applied to 80 independent Extremadura participants. Adding three-phonation log RAP/APQ3 dispersion to mean conventional and nonlinear acoustic measures increased Brier loss by 0.010235; source-refit/target-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.017390, 0.059527]. This test does not support incremental cross-cohort utility. Both models transferred poorly.
